summary: Brazil’s ecosystem pledges span restoration, conservation, agriculture and a cross-cutting deforestation objective. Restoration targets are 6 million forest hectares by 2030, a 12-million-hectare recovery target by 2030 and 24 million hectares by 2050. Brazil’s current forest cover is 4.42 million km² (51.9% of the country); as a scale reference, the 6-, 12- and 24-million-hectare figures are approximately 1.4%, 2.7% and 5.4% of that cover, respectively. The conservation pledge seeks a 1% per-year increase in technological and sustainable biodiversity use by industry. The cross-cutting Both commitment pursues zero deforestation by eliminating illegal deforestation and compensating for legal suppression of native vegetation, although no date is stated. The agriculture pledge calls for a 50% increase in biofuels’ share of the transport energy matrix, also without a stated date.
